en: One fascicle of the *Vajraśekhara-yoga Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-pūjā-vidhi*. Compiled by the Grand Master of the Household,
Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su.
I take refuge in the Youthful Mañjuśrī. Relying upon yoga, I shall explain the recitation of the vajra-activities of body, speech, and mind.
A practitioner of the profound three secrets of the Tathāgata should generate the mind of Samantabhadra and receive the vajra precepts from a master.
Disregarding one's own body and life, one should give rise to compassion; only then can one enter the wheel of liberation.
One should receive the *samaya* from the master, including the mudrās and secret mantras as explained in the sūtras.
One should revere the *ācārya* as if they were the Buddha, and maintain a heart of earnest devotion toward one’s fellow practitioners.
Whether in mountain retreats or *āraṇyakas*, by flowing springs, bathing pools, or pleasing trees;
on mountain peaks, in stone caves, or beside solitary trees— there one should establish a maṇḍala according to the ritual manual,
adorn the sacred chamber, place the principal deity therein, and dwell with single-minded devotion, making offerings according to one's means.
Universally beholding the oceans of Buddhas in the ten directions, one makes offerings and prostrates at the feet of all Tathāgatas to accomplish the vajra of the three karmas.
One should visualize the five wisdom vajras within the two hands, the tongue, and the heart; through this empowerment, all shall become *siddhi*.
Next, one should perform the mudrā named Awakening. With both hands forming vajra-fists, hook the thumbs and index fingers (tarjanī) together and extend the middle and ring fingers.
Rest the two little fingers on their sides to form the gesture of awakening.
The mantra for the true awakening is as follows: [mantra].
Homage to the Honored One Akṣobhya of the East. Casting off the body to entreat non-retrogression, one prostrates with the whole body touching the ground and pays homage with the heart.
Joining the vajra palms and extending them above the crown, one casts off the body to entreat the empowerment. The mantra is as follows:
Next, one should pay homage to the Honored One Ratnasambhava.
With palms joined in the vajra-mudrā at the heart, one should prostrate with the forehead touching the ground in devotion, surrendering the body to request the stage of empowerment.
The mantra for surrendering the body to request empowerment is as follows:
Next, pay homage to the Honored One, Lord Avalokiteśvara. To seek and request samādhi, join the palms like a vajra and place them upon the crown of the head;
then, with the mouth touching the ground, perform a sincere prostration.
The mantra for seeking and requesting samādhi by means of self-sacrifice is as follows:
Placing the vajra-pañjali at the heart, one offers up the body to request the wisdom-vajra of skillful means;
placing the vajra-pañjali at the heart, one prostrates by touching the crown of the head to the ground.
The mantra for offering up the body to request skillful means is as follows:
Next, again pay homage to the Buddhas of the ten directions. Visualize your body pervading before all the Buddhas and perform the prostration with the five limbs touching the ground.
Constantly forming the Vajra-samaya mudrā, the mantra for universally paying homage to the ten directions is as follows:

Next, recite the mantra for accomplishing the sublime: "May all Tathāgatas bestow their empowerment upon all sentient beings who seek supreme goals, swiftly causing them to accomplish the unsurpassed path.
The mantra for accomplishing the aims of all sentient beings is as follows:
Next, one should sit with legs crossed and the body upright, purifying the three karmas to make them stainless;
for the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure, may this body of mine be purified and free from defilement.
The mantra for purifying the three karmas is as follows:

Next, perform the Mañjuśrī-samaya mudrā: interlace the ten fingers to form a full moon, then extend the *kṣānti* (ring) and *praṇidhi* (little finger) straight upward like a vajra sword. Visualize one’s own body as being identical to Mañjughoṣa.
The samaya mantra is as follows: [Mantra]
Oṃ vajratricchaṇa samayas tvaṃ. Next, join the ten fingers of the hands in the vajra-palms gesture, with the first joints of the fingers interlaced.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ vajrāñjali svāhā. Having formed the *vajrabandha* by joining the palms of both hands together, recite this mantra:
Next, one should open the heart and enter the Buddha-wisdom.
One should visualize the two syllables *traṭ* at the two breasts, both white in color. Visualize these syllables as two door-panels;
with the two hands, one should form the Vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*) mudrā. By striking three times, the doors shall open at the heart.
The Heart Mantra for Delighting says:
One should contemplate the wondrous lotus as the gateway of the letter A. With the mudrā, summon [the deity] to enter the palace of the heart;
With concentration and wisdom, form the moon and the vajra-bind; Place the dhyāna and prajñā fingers in the palms and visualize the letter entering.
The mantra for entering the Vajra-syllable is as follows:
Next, one should form the seal of the heart-gate of the door.
As with the insignia of the previous entry-seal, bend the vajra-finger (forefinger) over the wisdom-finger (middle finger). Thus, one attains firmness and non-retrogression.
The mantra of the Vajra Fist is as follows:
Next, bind the Samaya of Samantabhadra. Because his essence is identical to the Sattva-vajra, the hands of concentration and wisdom are joined in the vajra-bind;
the two fingers of patience and aspiration are raised like a banner.
As soon as one recites the mantra of the original vow-seal, the body abides within a moon-disc.
The Samaya-mantra of the Sattva is as follows:
Next, bind the Samaya of Supreme Joy; with the hands of concentration and wisdom, form a firm lunar bond.
The union of patience and the vow of deliverance, with generosity, wisdom, meditation, and knowledge joined vertically,
is the mantra. Next,
bind the Vajra Trailokyavijaya mudrā and visualize one’s own body as being identical to it, without distinction.
Forming the two vajra-fists of śamatha and vipaśyanā, hook the thumbs and little fingers together, extend the index and middle fingers,
and turn to the right with the right hand to expel obstacles and establish the boundary to the right. Manifesting a form of wrathful majesty out of compassion,
the mantra of Trailokyavijaya is as follows:
Next, bind the Lotus Samaya mudrā. In order to bring the practice of contemplation to fulfillment, interlace the ten fingers to form a moon; join the thumbs and ring fingers upright and touching.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, perform the mudrā for summoning all the rākṣasas:
with the two hands of concentration and wisdom in the vajra-bond, join the ring fingers and thumbs like mountain peaks; extend the index and middle fingers like hooks.
The mantra for summoning the rākṣasas is as follows: [Mantra]

Next, bind the Vajra-Sin-Destroying Mudrā: join the three fingers of both hands together with the palms facing inward, interlace the fingers, and extend the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *anāmikā* (ring finger) upright like banners. With each recitation of the mantra, strike once;
visualize that all one's beginningless karmic offenses—numerous, naked, black, and resembling the forms of ghosts—are thus destroyed.
Recite that sublime mantra for destroying misdeeds, striking with the mudrā to cause them to be extinguished.
When the practitioner wishes to enter the vajra-samādhi, first abide in the mudrā of the sublime discerning wisdom:
interlace the two hands of wisdom and means with palms facing upward, and press the thumbs of the effort and meditative concentration fingers against each other.
By practicing meditative absorption (*samādhi*) with this sublime seal, one immediately attains the Tathāgata’s immovable wisdom.
Next, the practitioner enters the visualization of the four subtle vajras;
they should contemplate the inhalation and exhalation as being white, like the color of milk.
When the light at the tip of one's own nose becomes brilliantly pure,
one should know that it transforms into a five-pronged vajra according to its distance;
this vajra enters through the nose and pervades the entire body.
Recite this mantra:
Oṃ sūkṣma-vajra. Then visualize this vajra as gradually extending and gradually expanding until it pervades the entire dharmadhātu.
Recite this mantra: Oṃ sphara vajra.
Then recite the subsequent mantra again, gradually withdrawing and contracting [the visualization] until its extent is equal to one's own body.
The mantra is: Oṃ saṃhara vajra. Furthermore, by empowering with this mantra, one causes it to remain firm and not disperse.
The mantra is:
Oṃ dharṇi tiṣṭha vajra. Then, one enters the visualization of the four immeasurable minds (catvāry apramāṇāni).
First, one enters the meditative concentration of immeasurable loving-kindness (*maitrī-apramāṇa*).
With a profound and pure mind, one universally contemplates the six realms and four modes of birth;
all sentient beings are endowed with the *tathāgatagarbha*.
May I be endowed with the three vajras of body, speech, and mind;
through the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets,
may all sentient beings likewise [be so endowed].
Having observed in this manner, as Samantabhadra Bodhisattva did, one should immediately recite the mantra of the *Mahāmaitrī-samādhi*:
Oṃ mahā-maitry-ātmaka svāhā. Next, one should enter the immeasurable mind of compassion (*karuṇā*).
With the wisdom of samādhi and a heart of compassion,
he universally contemplates the six realms and four modes of birth;
all sentient beings are submerged in the ocean of suffering of saṃsāra.
Failing to realize one's own mind,
they give rise to false discrimination and various secondary afflictions; therefore,
they do not penetrate the equality of True Suchness (tathatā).
Just as space transcends the virtues of the sands of the Ganges,
through the power of my cultivation of the three secrets and their empowerment,
may all sentient beings likewise [attain this].
Having observed in this manner, the Bodhisattva Ākāśagarbha then recited the mantra of the Great Compassion Samādhi:
*Oṃ mahākāruṇika-ārya-sphara*. Next, one should enter the wisdom of the samādhi of immeasurable joy.
With a pure mind, one universally contemplates the six realms and four modes of birth.
All sentient beings are originally pure;
their lotus-like minds remain unstained.
The adventitious defilements are by nature pure.
By the power of the merit of my cultivation of the three secrets, may all sentient beings become equal to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Having visualized thus:
Then, one should recite the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Joy:
*Oṃ jñānapramodasphara*. Next, one should enter the wisdom of the samādhi of the immeasurable mind of equanimity (*upekṣā*).
With a mind of equanimity, one universally contemplates the six realms and the four modes of birth.
All sentient beings are devoid of "I" and "mine," free from the aggregates,
elements, and sense bases, and liberated from the grasped and the grasper.
The mind of equality regarding all phenomena is fundamentally unarisen,
for their nature and characteristics are empty;
this is due to the power of the merit I have cultivated through the three secrets.
Having thus contemplated that all sentient beings are equal to the treasury of space,
the Bodhisattva recites the mantra of the Samādhi of Great Equanimity: Oṃ mahāpeśā-sphara-yogin.
By practicing the meditative concentrations of the four immeasurables and reciting the mantras of the four immeasurables,
all various demonic activities, karmic obstacles, and difficulties of humans and devas in future ages shall be entirely eliminated.
Within the body, immeasurable merit is suddenly accumulated;
the mind becomes gathered, pliant, capable, and masterful.
The practitioner should cultivate the āsphānaka-dhyāna.
One who practices this dharma remains motionless in their limbs and ceases the inhalation and exhalation,
making them so subtle as not to allow for distraction.
One should then visualize all Buddhas in the void of space,
filling the ten directions like sesame seeds;
with a vajra-snap of the fingers, they address the practitioner, saying:
"Good son, observe your original mind.
Having heard this, the practitioner immediately visualizes himself prostrating at the feet of all Buddhas, performing the salutation universally.
The mantra is: Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāmanomayakalpe pratiṣṭha.
Contemplating the fundamental mind, he addressed the Buddhas, saying:
Since the characteristics of the mind have no substantiality, how can one cultivate and realize it?
The Buddhas say to the practitioner:
"Good son, contemplate the moon-disc within the mind as being like a light mist."
Then, one should recite the *Vimala-bodhi-mantra* and contemplate the *Cittacandra-mantra*, which says:
*Oṃ citra-prativedha-vicintya-kāruṇi*. The practitioner should contemplate this clearly and with focused attention.
Before long, you shall behold the pure bodhicitta,
free from all dust and defilements, as pure as the full moon.
Then, recite the mantra of bodhicitta:
Oṃ vṛddhicittam utpādayāmi. One should visualize the syllable *daṃ* within the moon of bodhicitta;
it is brilliant like gold, shining with great radiance like the sun.
It immediately transforms into the sword of the Prajñāpāramitā,
the wisdom-sword capable of severing afflictions by transcending all conceptual discrimination.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ tiṣṭha khaga. Visualize that the sword of wisdom gradually increases in size until it pervades the entire dharmadhātu.
The mantra is: Oṃ sphara khaga. Visualize that the sword of wisdom is gradually withdrawn until it is equal in size to one's own body. The mantra is:
Oṃ saṃhara krodha-īśvara-jñāna-khaḍga dṛḍha-mā vilaya! Recite the mantra again:
Oṃ nṛtya tiṣṭha krodha. Visualize the Tathāgata in the sky.
All enter the sword of wisdom and become one body.
Contemplate in this way: "Just as the essential nature of those Buddhas is such, mine is likewise so."
The mantra is: Oṃ samaya-hūṃ | mahā-samaya-hūṃ | sarva-tathāgata-abhiṣeka-āgata-mukuṭa-hūṃ | Contemplate that the sword of wisdom gradually transforms into the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
Possessing a body of great majesty and virtue, he is adorned with various kinds of necklaces and ornaments;
visualize five topknots upon his head.
His right hand holds the sword of wisdom, and his left hand grasps a blue lotus.
Upon the flower is a case containing the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra;
his body is the color of saffron.
Recite the mantra *A-ra-pa-ca-na* once in your mind.
Next, form the Vajra-Wisdom-Sword Mudrā: interlace the hands in the manner of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā*, with the thumbs and ring fingers extended upward like the shape of a sword.
By sealing the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head, one accomplishes the protection of the body.
The mantra of the fundamental deity is as follows: [Mantra]
Next, bind the seal of Mañjuśrī’s Five Topknots: The two hands of śamatha and vipaśyanā interlace externally;
the thumbs (dāna) and index fingers (prajñā) join together like a peak. The middle fingers (vīrya), ring fingers (praṇidhāna), and little fingers (kṣānti) touch their heads together;
the thumbs (jñāna) and little fingers (dhyāna) join their heads together. One should then recite the fundamental wondrous mantra.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, the practitioner forms the Single Topknot Seal (*ekajaṭāmudrā*). Interlace the two hands of concentration and wisdom with their palms facing inward;
join the *kṣānti* and *praṇidhi* fingers together like a banner, supporting one another to form a circle resembling a topknot.
The One-Syllable Mantra is as follows:
Next, the practitioner forms the Three-Tuft Seal (Trijaṭā-mudrā). The fingers of the ten perfections—stopping, contemplation, and so forth—are joined at the heart;
the index and middle fingers are extended while the ring and little fingers are bent into the palms, causing their middle joints to support one another.
The three-syllable mantra is as follows:

Next, join the palms of meditative concentration and wisdom with hollowed hands; interlace the fire-wheels (middle fingers) and hold them, while the two water-wheels (ring fingers) and wind-rings (index fingers) are bent like the great void. Its form is like a hook, forming the secret mudrā.
And by applying [the mantra] universally to one's own limbs, one then performs all various activities.
The root mantra of the Dharmakāya of the Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva is as follows:
Next, one should perform the consecration and form the Jewel Seal (*ratnamudrā*):

interlace the two hands to form the crescent moon, bend the index fingers inward in the shape of a jewel, and join the tips of the thumbs and little fingers below, placing them upon the forehead and parting the hair on both sides;
then, form the Wisdom Fist (*jñānamuṣṭi*) as if tying a silk scarf.
Slowly open both hands forward; one should know that this is the mantra for binding the stainless silk ribbon.
Next, bind the jewel-sword and perform self-consecration: join the two palms and bend the forefingers.
Both *dhyāna* and *prajñā* are bent and placed within the palms; positioned upon the forehead, they are divided into two sides.
The *Abhiṣeka-mantra* says:
Next, again form the Armor Seal (*kavaca-mudrā*), with both hands making vajra-fists.
Place it before the heart and extend the power of progress; visualize the syllable OṂ twice on the left and right, imagining a stream of green light.
It revolves three times before the heart, then behind the back, reaching down to the navel and the two knees; it revolves again to the navel and circles behind the waist.
From the waist to the heart, rotate the two shoulders; from the shoulders to the throat, turn toward the back of the neck;
again, from the back of the neck to the front of the forehead; from the forehead to the crown of the head, form the *jñānamuṣṭi* (wisdom-fist), then slowly release it downward like a hanging sash.
This rotation of *śamatha* and *vipaśyanā* is like the movement of a dance.
The mantra for the Full Moon Armor, formed by interlacing the two hands, is as follows:
Oṃ vajrakavaca varikuru vajravajra haṃ. Next is the ritual for clapping the vajra palms.
Clap the two hands together twice and then three times; by performing the mudrā and reciting the mantra, one can cause the assembly of noble beings to rejoice.
To swiftly attain the joyful essence of the deity, the mantra of joy is as follows:
Next, bind the Great Ocean Seal: cross the two hands inward with palms facing upward at the navel;
the thumbs and index fingers touch slightly.
The mantra is as follows:

The ten fingers of concentration and wisdom are interlaced within; the two arms are raised together with the elbows joined at the heart, held upright while reciting the mantra. This is called the Seal of the Precious Mountain Sumeru.
The mantra is as follows:

Next, bind the Great Seal of the Vajra Wheel: form vajra fists with both hands, interlocking the *tarjanī* (forefinger) and *madhyamā* (middle finger) of the right and left hands respectively. As for the mantra for the four places of the body at that mandala, it is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the four means of attraction; one should recite the four-syllable mantra.

Furthermore, bind the Vajrapuruṣa mudrā: join the hands in the manner of śamatha and vipaśyanā, with the outer fingers interlaced, and bend the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* fingers into the palms. Presenting this mudrā can cause the Great Sage to appear.
The mantra is as follows:
Without releasing the previous mudrā, recite the mantra; this will enable the practitioner to see the mantra clearly.
The mantra is as follows:
Furthermore, having bound the samaya and recited the mantra following the great mudrā of the Vajra Sword, the mantra for oneself and the deity is as follows:
Next, bind the four secret seals; recite these vajra syllables followed by the four-syllable vidyā-mantra: *hrīḥ haṃ vaṃ hoḥ*.
As before, at the four places, [recite] *hraḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*. Next, with the Vajrarāja, summon the assembly of all noble beings.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, the practitioner should visualize before their seat an eight-petaled lotus with stamens and filaments, serving as a lion throne atop Mount Sumeru for meditative insight and calm abiding;
upon this throne, there is further a pavilion made of the seven precious jewels.

Visualize within [yourself] the king of seven-jeweled lotuses; above it, visualize the syllable *TAM*, possessing majestic radiance that illuminates the entire dharma-realm without exception. This syllable transforms into a sharp vajra;
observe it clearly and precisely as its original form. Summon the Bodhisattvas and visualize them entering your body.
With the two hands formed like a crescent hook, visualize one’s own body as being identical to that Bodhisattva.
Next, bind the Great Seal of the Vajra Hook (*vajrāṅkuśa-mahāmudrā*):
with the wisdom of summoning all Tathāgatas, the concentration and wisdom [fingers] are joined, the outer fingers interlaced, and the *pāramitā* finger bent like a hook, alone triple-curved.
The mantra of Vajrasattva is as follows:
Next, bind the Great Seal of the Vajra Lasso. To draw [the deity] into the body and realize the wisdom-body:
join the palms in the posture of meditative concentration (dhyāna-mudrā), with the fingers of the thumbs and little fingers interlaced like the shape of a ring.
Next, one should bind the cord and enter the body of the Honored One.
By binding the moon and the deity of dhyāna-knowledge within the palms, through the empowerment of this secret mudrā, they are transformed into a single entity without distinction.
The mantra of the Vajra-cord is as follows:

Next, bind the Vajra Hook-Chain Mudrā: By joining the Wisdom and Action fingers with the Vigor and Strength fingers in a hooking fashion, one causes the deity to remain firm. This is called the Vajra Capable-Stopping Mudrā;
next, the Chain Mudrā should be made firm, forming four loops like a ring on the four days of the moon.
By the power of this mudrā, all [elements] are made firm and unchanging.
The mantra of the Vajra-Chain is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the Sublime Sound of Vajra; it is able to cause all the noble ones to rejoice.
The thumb and index finger (jñāna-muṣṭi) are bent into the vajra-bind; this is called the Vajra-ānanda-mudrā.
Next, bind the bell-mudrā to bring about joy: the thumb and index finger enter the palms like a small bell, causing the Honored One and the assembly to all rejoice.
Through this empowerment, swift and wondrous accomplishment is attained.
The mantra of the Vajra Bell is:
Oṃ khaṭa khaṭa. Next, one should visualize holding the arghya perfumed water with both hands and offering it, thereby washing the feet of the Great Holy One, Vajrāyudha Bodhisattva, and his retinue.
Alternatively, empower the argha with the hundred-syllable mantra and offer it.
The mantra is as follows:
Next, form the Mañjuśrī-karma-mudrā: with both hands, form vajra-fists.
Place the samādhi-feather upon one’s own heart; the wisdom-feather is like the posture of grasping a sword.
By the power of this excellent seal of ritual action (*karmamudrā*), one’s body becomes indistinguishable from that of the deity.
The *karma-mantra* is as follows:
Next, bind the seal of the Vajra Sharp Sword: bind the seal and extend the *tarjanī* and *anāmikā* fingers like a sword.
Through the empowerment of this sublime seal, one shall obtain the profound wisdom of Prajñā.
The mantra of the Vajra Sharp Sword is as follows:
Next, bind the wondrous mudrā of the blue lotus: join the *kṣānti* (ring) fingers with the *dāna* (middle) and *prajñā* (little) fingers to form the wondrous banner;

cross the *vīrya* (forefinger) and *praṇidhāna* (thumb) fingers over the backs of the *śīla* (index) fingers; bend the *vīrya* and *bala* (forefinger) fingers inward to pinch the *dhyāna* and *jñāna* (little fingers).
The mantra of the blue lotus is as follows:
Next, bind the mudrā of the Peacock King’s Seat: Interlace the two hands of Samādhi and Prajñā within;
extend the thumbs and ring fingers together so that they resemble the shape of a tail; join the middle and little fingers like a head.
The mantra of the Peacock King’s Seat is as follows:
Namo buddhāya | Namo dharmāya | Next, perform the inner offering of playful joy.
Bind the hands in the *dhyāna-mudrā* and join the *jñāna-aṅguṣṭha* (wisdom thumbs) while extending the other fingers;
through the empowerment of this seal, may the *dānapāramitā* be swiftly fulfilled.
The mantra of Vajralāsyā is as follows.

Next, perform the offering by forming the Vajramālā mudrā. By extending the arms straight according to the previous *lāsya* [dance] and consecrating through the binding of this seal, one shall fulfill the perfection of pure ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*).
The mantra of Vajramālā is as follows:
Next, form the mudrā of Vajragīti. Let the garland hang down from the navel to the mouth, and by forming the mudrā of Vajragīti, one swiftly attains the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā).
The mantra for the Vajra Song is as follows:

Next, perform the offering of the Vajra Dance. By forming the two fists and rotating them in the manner of a dance, through the power of the empowerment of this dance mudrā, one swiftly fulfills the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*).
The mantra for the Vajra Dance is as follows:
Next, form the seal of the outer vajra offering; bind it at the heart and then release it downward.
By the power of forming this incense seal, one shall realize the perfection of meditative concentration (dhyāna-pāramitā).
The mantra of Vajradhūpa is as follows:

Next, bind the Vajrapuṣpāñjali mudrā. By binding the mudrā and then releasing it upward like scattering flowers, through the empowerment of the Vajrapuṣpāñjali mudrā, one swiftly realizes Prajñāpāramitā.
The mantra for scattering flowers with the vajra is as follows:

Next, form the Vajra-Lamp Seal. By binding the hands externally and joining the *dhyāna* and *prajñā* fingers like a banner, through the formation of the Vajra-Lamp Seal, one shall attain the *upāya-pāramitā*.
The mantra of Vajrapradīpa is as follows:
Next, bind the seal of Vajragandha. With the moon at the breast, scatter [the fingers] like anointing with perfume;
by binding this seal of Vajragandha and performing its empowerment, one swiftly fulfills the perfection of the vow.
The mantra for Vajra-unguent is:
Oṃ su-gandhāṅgi. Next, the practitioner should recite the one hundred and eight names of the Great Holy Mañjuśrī.
Praising the immeasurable virtues of the tutelary deity and the assembly of noble ones, he says: *Ārya-śākyamuni-paranirvṛtāgatāya namaḥ*.
1. *Siddham abhyatāṅkārīṇām* 2. *Śrī-ajita-sarvāhitijāgatipraṇidhita* (or *praṇidhita*) (Note:
The transcription provided contains several phonetic markers and archaic transliteration conventions typical of Sanskrit manuscripts rendered into Chinese characters.
The reconstructed Sanskrit above reflects the most probable reading based on standard Buddhist terminology.)
Āḥ trajaṭa ṭuṇṭuṇḍa ḍombi nagnāḥ | satyavāca-kṣama-bhīr-avahita-citta maitrā || 2 ||
Hara sanna nārātaye | Siddhivāgvibodhanī sujane sunāyakamale siddhim uccara | Mantre vare sannatuṣṭi || 6–8 ||

Having recited the praises, the practitioner binds the root and other mudrās and forms the visualization of [the deity] as being added to their own body.
Together with the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī,
one should recite the Vajra-hundred-syllable mantra while not releasing this mudrā.
Even if one has committed various kinds of evil karma throughout past lives, [it shall be purified].
All obstacles of sin, including the five deeds of immediate retribution,
are entirely extinguished through the empowerment of this hundred-syllable mantra.
Upon seeing the body, one attains the Śūraṅgama-samādhi.
If the mind is distracted, one should recite this mantra repeatedly—
whether seven times, twenty-one times, thirty-seven times, or even up to one hundred and eight times.
One will swiftly attain union with samādhi.
The hundred-syllable mantra is as follows: Oṃ kha-ga-sattva samayam anupālaya.

13. *Āṭa-ke-gama-mukha-vāma-samaya-sattva-aḥ*. This mantra possesses great power.
If a practitioner violates the samaya,
their contemplation becomes disordered,
or they commit transgressions due to mental dullness or agitation.
By means of empowering through the repeated recitation of this mantra,
one can cause the practitioner to be endowed with supreme merit,
thereby compensating for previous transgressions, rectifying failures, and increasing their spiritual gains.
The majestic power swiftly accords with samādhi.
Without dispersing the previous mudrā,
gaze intently at the presence of the deity before you.
Furthermore, one should clearly and precisely visualize oneself as being no different from the deity.
Moreover, this mudrā should be placed at the heart.
He then recited the five-syllable dhāraṇī:
"A-ra-pa-ca-na. The practitioner [should do so] with vajra-speech.
Alternatively, using the Lotus Speech,
one should recite this five-syllable mantra clearly and distinctly seven times, or twenty-one times.
Perform the empowerment upon the four places with the mudrā of scattering;
then, taking the rosary and coiling it within the palms,
empower it seven times with the Thousand-Turn Mantra.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajrayakṣiye jvālamaye hūṃ. Then, with both hands, hold the rosary.
Abiding in the samādhi of the deity before one's heart,
recite [the mantra] neither too slowly nor too quickly,
either one hundred and eight times.
Whether it be one thousand or even ten thousand times,
once the count of recitations is complete,
hold the rosary with both hands and place it upon the crown of the head.
Thereafter, place [the image] back in its original location.
If one is performing recitation through meditative concentration (*samādhi*),
one should visualize the Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom within the mind.
Visualize the five syllables clearly arranged within it, contemplating them with precise clarity.
In accordance with their meaning, let the mind merge with the Prajñāpāramitā;
this is called the samādhi recitation.
If the body becomes weary or lax,
one should immediately form the sword mudrā of the Honored One and recite the five-syllable mantra seven times.
Furthermore, one should make offerings to all Buddhas with the eight great offerings,
extolling and praising them with sublime words and phrases,
and presenting argha water.
Next, with the seal of the three periods of time, rotate it clockwise to dissolve the boundary.
Then, bind the seal of the Vajra Sharp Sword and escort the various holy ones back to their respective palaces.
The mantra for dismissal is as follows:
OṂ KṚTVA SARVASATTVARĀTASIDDHIDATTA ĀYAN TAKTU PIṄGALACCHADVAṂ MUDHAVIŚYAMA PUṆARĀGA MA NAYĀTO OṂ VAJRATIṢṬHA MUḤ. Having performed this rite, [proceed].
Furthermore, empower it by reciting the samaya-mudrā mantra while sealing the four locations with the mudrā;
thereafter, perform the consecration.
Donning the adamantine armor,
perform the fourfold prostrations as before to the Buddhas of the four directions,
followed by the confession of faults, the making of vows, and so forth.
Thereafter, one should resort to a secluded and quiet place,
adorn it with fragrant flowers, abide in the samādhi of the deity,
and recite all the Vaipulya Mahāyāna sūtras, such as the Great Chapter of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.
Up to the *Mañjuśrī-prajñā* and other such sūtras,
one may practice walking meditation as desired.
Regarding the two characters of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*, one should cultivate them with diligence throughout the four periods of day and night.
One attains the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*) in this very life and shall realize perfect enlightenment after sixteen lifetimes.
The mantra of Mañjuśrī-krodha is:
*Oṃ vajratikṣṇa kuru dhākinī hūṃ phaṭ*. This mantra is used for protecting the body, expelling obstructors, and establishing the boundary (*sīmā-bandha*).
One may also obtain pure incense, flowers, and all other ritual implements;

one should then make this aspiration: "May all sentient beings encounter this teaching, May Mañjuśrī always serve as their spiritual friend, May they swiftly realize the skillful wisdom of Prajñāpāramitā, And quickly become the Unsurpassed Honored One among two-legged beings."
